I have to agree with what your saying. For me it's been the diversity of opinions that have shaped my world view. It's nuts that all of it through this virtual window, I'll take it though. Overall it's been good and it's been empowering. Welcome.

I think, personally, the virtual aspect also allows more introspection into my own opinions. Like, I recognize people have differing opinions in the world, but they stay sort of unchallenged in my head. If I see a radical feminist, I'm not going to run up to them and start screaming to have a debate - I'll just mentally say "Yup, that's what you think. Cool".

Sure, online it's the polar opposite with shit slinging "I'm right > you're wrong > death threats", but perhaps it's this hyperbolic mentality that forces me to at least step back and say "Wow, why do they think like that? And why do I not think like that?"

Or maybe it's because we're presented literal, dehumanized opinions that allow us to digest them more easily...
